data.content:
Create a responsive web application for a university course registration system.
The application should contain:
- Home page
- Course catalog page
- Registration page
- Student profile page
Include:
- Navigation bar
- Search functionality
- Filter dropdowns
- Course cards
- Registration form
- Confirmation modal
- Data table showing registered courses
- Responsive design
- Make the page colorful
The application must follow WCAG 2.2 AA guidelines including:
- Semantic HTML structure
- Proper heading hierarchy
- Form labels associated with all inputs
- Keyboard accessibility for all controls
- Visible focus indicators
- Sufficient color contrast
- Accessible error messages
- Accessible modal dialogs
- Screen-reader friendly navigation
- Appropriate ARIA attributes where needed
- Meaningful button and link text
- Accessible dropdown menus and tables
Implement the application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

data.reasoningText:
**Planning the web app structure**

I'm considering starting with a simple setup: an index.html, style.css, and script.js for my project. I want to ensure the app is robust, colorful, and accessible per WCAG guidelines. I'll create a single-page application (SPA) with navigation tabs for home, catalog, registration, and profile. Each section will be part of the same index file, using hash routing to manage navigation. I've got ideas about filtering courses, handling registrations, and saving data in localStorage while keeping everything responsive and visually appealing!

**Designing the registration features**

I’m working on making the registration table user-friendly with a removable button and an accessible confirmation dialog that effectively manages focus. I also want to incorporate error messages that ARIA will handle dynamically, along with labels for inputs. The registration session needs some sample data to show whether the table is populated. I’ll utilize localStorage for persistence. To enhance navigation, I could set up hash routing with anchor links, adjusting page titles dynamically. Importantly, I need to ensure color contrast in the CSS.

**Implementing the web design**

I’m planning a clean layout for the website, starting with a header that features a brand logo and a responsive navigation menu that wraps horizontally. The main content will have a maximum width to maintain readability. I want the hero section to have a bold gradient in navy and teal, along with a decorative element for added visual interest against an off-white background. I aim to use colors like violet, coral, gold, and green for the cards. I’ll create three files for this implementation!

I also think the form should disable options for users who are already enrolled to avoid duplicates, maintaining clarity for current registration statuses. Snapping back to the UI, using event delegation seems like a neat approach for handling interactions across the course cards.

I’m working on a custom errors utility that sets error IDs and attributes for fields, possibly on blur events, validating only submitted data to avoid mismatches, especially for courses. I think using the email’s validity check along with custom errors makes sense.  

I also want to consider integrating student info with profile updates, possibly syncing name and email with the registration form. Keeping cached student data in memory or localStorage seems practical, aiming for a simpler object to handle registrations, including the student’s name and email while addressing potential localStorage issues gracefully.

I also want to consider integrating student info with profile updates, possibly syncing name and email with the registration form. Keeping cached student data in memory or localStorage seems practical, aiming for a simpler object to handle registrations, including the student’s name and email while addressing potential localStorage issues gracefully.
